statusMeaning.implemented: A runnable harness check exists; its scope is limited to the stated assertion.
statusMeaning.planned: Acceptance requirement only; not executed or counted as passed by CI.

cases.given: The committed acceptance catalog
cases.when: A case is added or marked implemented
cases.then: IDs are unique, phase/risk/status are valid, assertions are nonempty and an implemented test reference resolves.

cases.given: Pinned ILM 2.19.0 source evidence
cases.when: CI checks the snapshots
cases.then: Each content SHA-256 and Git blob ID matches sources.json and only the declared snapshot files are present.

cases.given: Public contributor code
cases.when: The CI workflow is evaluated
cases.then: Only approved unprivileged events, hosted runners, read permissions and SHA-pinned Actions are used, with no secrets or management network runners.

cases.given: The public repository working tree
cases.when: Fixtures or local configuration are added
cases.then: Private key blocks, common credential tokens and disallowed local/lab artifacts are rejected; synthetic fixture names use reserved examples.

cases.given: The independent 2.19.0 route subset
cases.when: The official SDK reports its Entity Provider endpoints
cases.then: Each required method and route is advertised and reachable through the actual SDK handler using a test provider.

cases.given: SDK explicitly configured for the v1 family
cases.when: Info and health are requested
cases.then: GET /v1 advertises the entityProvider group and GET /v1/health returns the v1 status shape.

cases.given: Six pinned 2.19.0 DTO source files
cases.when: The SDK serializable DTO field sets are inspected
cases.then: Declared JSON fields match the independent Java field names, including no invented chain field in push.

cases.given: Synthetic v3 RequestAttribute payloads containing operation correlation
cases.when: CSR and push DTOs are decoded and re-encoded
cases.then: Base64 payloads and the entire attribute content survive without being dropped or replaced; legacy v2 content compatibility remains unproven.

cases.given: Malformed JSON and a test provider not-found error
cases.when: Requests reach the SDK HTTP boundary
cases.then: The boundary returns 400 or 404 respectively with a v1 errors envelope rather than a v2 problem shape.

cases.given: Three 2.19.0 per-entity validators annotated 204
cases.when: The pinned SDK handles successful validation
cases.then: The observed SDK 200 responses remain explicitly listed as K-001; this check does not waive the target 204 contract.

cases.given: A push request missing its required certificate field
cases.when: The SDK decodes the body
cases.then: The request fails before the test provider can receive a push call.

cases.given: Strict HTTP decoding and a generated SDK DTO
cases.when: An extra JSON property is supplied
cases.then: The current AdditionalProperties behavior is characterized explicitly; future application allowlisting must be separately tested.

cases.given: The implemented connector and an actual ILM 2.19.0 instance
cases.when: Registration, attributes, Location detail and native lifecycle calls execute
cases.then: Info/auth/validation status and field semantics are accepted by Core, with K-001 resolved or evidence-backed tolerance documented.

cases.given: A connector boundary around the real SDK handler
cases.when: Info, health and all attribute validators execute
cases.then: The v1 shapes remain intact; three per-entity validators return target 204 while kind validation retains 200.

cases.given: Approved canonical v3 string attribute requests
cases.when: Entity create/update, Location, CSR and push requests are decoded
cases.then: Valid wire requests reach the test backend once; this does not assert device or issuance semantics.

cases.given: A per-entity attribute validation response
cases.when: The next handler succeeds or returns 400/403/422/500
cases.then: Only successful 200 becomes bodyless 204; errors including actual SDK validation errors are preserved.

cases.given: Backend errors rendered by the configured SDK
cases.when: 400/403/404/422/500 errors cross the boundary
cases.then: The v1 message, authentication or validation-array shape is preserved without v2 fields.

cases.given: Untrusted v3 request attributes at every used nesting level
cases.when: Unknown, duplicate, missing, null, mismatched UUID/name, v2 or reference content is submitted
cases.then: Invalid attributes return a v1 422 array before any backend call.

cases.given: Operator-approved targets, entity bindings and staging pools
cases.when: A request changes device/target, supplies a command-like Trustpoint, overrides scope or requests removal
cases.then: The boundary rejects the request before the backend; future adapters and durable ownership checks remain separate acceptance.

cases.given: Malformed, duplicate, trailing, invalid UTF-8, deeply nested or oversized JSON
cases.when: The HTTP boundary parses the body independently of SDK models
cases.then: The request is rejected with 400 or 413 and zero backend calls.

cases.given: Encoded/cleaned route aliases, query overrides, wrong methods or unsupported media
cases.when: The request reaches the boundary before SDK routing
cases.then: The boundary returns an explicit v1 error without redirecting or calling the backend.

cases.given: Invalid operator targets/names, mutable policy inputs or failed entity resolution
cases.when: The boundary is constructed or resolves a device binding
cases.then: Unsafe policy is rejected, accepted policy is copied, and resolver errors fail closed without leaking details.

cases.given: Concurrent valid requests sharing one immutable policy
cases.when: Thirty-two requests pass through the boundary
cases.then: Every request reaches the backend once; the hosted race detector also checks concurrent access.

cases.given: Untrusted push envelopes and certificate wire values
cases.when: Unknown fields, invented chain, wrong type, null or malformed Base64 are supplied
cases.then: Invalid wire requests never reach the backend; X.509 semantics remain a later lifecycle check.

cases.given: An approved literal IPv6 device and a cancelled request context
cases.when: A valid entity is created or a context-aware resolver fails
cases.then: Approved canonical IPv6 is accepted and a resolver failure cannot reach the backend.

cases.given: A real temporary SQLite store and the SDK handler
cases.when: Entities are created, renamed, reopened and deleted
cases.then: Entity and HTTPS service identities persist; duplicates and device rebinding fail; deletion removes only metadata.

cases.given: Complete synthetic public certificate observations
cases.when: The read-only provider returns Location detail and Info
cases.then: Multiple entries and observed key association are reported without key-management or renewal capability; unsupported calls return 501 without reader side effects.

cases.given: An absent adapter, failed/incomplete observation or invalid certificate
cases.when: Location inventory is requested
cases.then: The provider fails explicitly; only a confirmed complete empty observation is an empty success, and transcript details do not leak.

cases.given: Pinned 2.19.0 attribute source and connector definitions
cases.when: Kind, Entity and Location definitions cross the SDK HTTP boundary
cases.then: Required v3 data definitions use numeric version 3, decode through SDK discriminators, omit unavailable capabilities, and validate Location attributes with 204.

cases.given: Two actual database handles and concurrent registrations
cases.when: Requests register the same device or the store closes/corrupts
cases.then: Exactly one persistent binding is created and storage failures never become successful empty results or reset the database.

cases.given: Operator configuration and an existing Entity binding
cases.when: Unknown/inline configuration or a changed device target is supplied
cases.then: Strict configuration rejects unsafe input and an existing Entity cannot silently move to another target.

cases.given: The actual SQLite entity database
cases.when: Durability pragmas and future schema versions are inspected
cases.then: WAL and FULL are verified; unsupported schemas and relative database paths fail closed.

cases.given: An existing entity in a real database
cases.when: SQLite denies a rename and a delete context is cancelled
cases.then: Neither failed operation changes the durable entity after close and reopen.

cases.given: A device with only some supported YANG nodes
cases.when: Capabilities are assessed
cases.then: Read/import/CSR/switch/save capabilities are evaluated separately and unsupported operations cannot be invoked.

cases.given: Read-only discovery through both adapters
cases.when: Success, parse failures and retries occur
cases.then: The complete command/RPC log contains no configuration, key generation, enrollment, import, protocol enablement or save operation.

cases.given: Synthetic PEM output containing leaf and CA certificates with multiple Trustpoints
cases.when: Inventory is parsed
cases.then: Every public certificate is decoded and attributed correctly without inferring activity from certificate order.

cases.given: Different certificate inventory and HTTPS binding state
cases.when: The Location is built
cases.then: Exactly one HTTPS active binding is identified and inactive/staged/rollback roles remain distinct.

cases.given: Truncated PEM, paging, CLI errors, invalid XML or an unknown format
cases.when: Discovery parses the response
cases.then: It reports incomplete or unsupported evidence and never silently fabricates an empty healthy inventory or write capability.

cases.given: A synthetic collector, real temporary SQLite and the SDK handler
cases.when: A Location is queried with complete, partial or timed-out evidence
cases.then: DER is deduplicated with all Trustpoint roles in v3 metadata; errors return 502/504 and no device write is enabled.

cases.given: A reader bound to approved target and explicit fingerprint assignments
cases.when: An ID, address, secret reference, host identity or role pool differs
cases.then: The read is refused before collection and caller mutations cannot change copied ownership evidence.

cases.given: Ambiguous XML and unapproved or stale role assignments
cases.when: Inventory semantics are checked independently of transport success
cases.then: Duplicate required data, foreign namespaces, excessive depth and invalid assignments expose no partial inventory.

cases.given: Multiple concurrent reads of the same immutable public evidence
cases.when: Inventories are parsed repeatedly under the race detector
cases.then: Evidence and assignments remain immutable and every read has one complete result.

cases.given: A synthetic SSH server and an approved management target
cases.when: Local lab readiness executes
cases.then: Only clock, NTP, privilege, filtered protocol configuration and HTTPS state reads are sent; unapproved targets are rejected.

cases.given: A synthetic TLS server and a public certificate learned through trusted SSH
cases.when: An independent TLS baseline handshake runs
cases.then: Exact DER and hostname must match, CA trust is recorded separately, cancellation fails and no application payload is sent.

cases.given: Synthetic inventory, readiness and independent TLS evidence
cases.when: The report evaluates required observations for approved CLI reads
cases.then: Writable account privilege does not block fixed reads; AAA denial stops collection and a failed repeat cannot prove stability.

cases.given: An absolute private directory or a path inside a Git checkout
cases.when: A lab report is persisted
cases.then: Evidence is created exclusively outside checkouts and existing reports cannot be overwritten.

cases.given: A synthetic SSH peer allowing only one exec channel per connection
cases.when: All five inventory commands execute
cases.then: Every command gets one independently pinned connection without retries or a shell.

cases.given: A synthetic self-signed CA and identical general-purpose display pair
cases.when: The explicit alias is parsed with an independent binding
cases.then: The DER is deduplicated while preserving CA and identity purposes; activity is never inferred from order.

cases.given: HTTPS status with authentication retry fields and wrapped cipher names
cases.when: The active binding is validated
cases.then: Known wrapped fields are accepted and unrecognized continuations cannot hide conflicting binding evidence.

cases.given: Private captured public replies with explicit exec completion evidence
cases.when: An offline parser replay runs
cases.then: Completed reads can be revalidated but incomplete wire execution cannot be promoted or claimed as live acceptance.

cases.given: An approved privilege-15 identity and unsynchronized clock
cases.when: CLI-only or NETCONF-and-CLI scope is selected explicitly
cases.then: CLI reads can pass with NTP recorded for the next live test; selected NETCONF is attempted even with empty CLI filter output and missing models prevent its PASS.

cases.given: A complete recorded live-format report and explicit operator-approved scope
cases.when: Acceptance is reassessed without network access
cases.then: A new private hash-linked assessment preserves the original report; failures, scope conflicts, incomplete reads, writes or inconsistent TLS evidence cannot be promoted.

cases.given: Synthetic NETCONF revisions, PKI/binding replies and independent CLI/TLS evidence
cases.when: NETCONF-and-CLI acceptance is evaluated
cases.then: Matching model evidence passes; missing revisions or a contradictory NETCONF binding prevent PASS.

cases.given: A pinned SSH host identity
cases.when: A different host key is presented
cases.then: The connection fails before authentication or commands; no automatic trust-on-first-use or insecure fallback occurs.

cases.given: AAA denies an operational command or RPC
cases.when: The adapter receives denial
cases.then: It reports permission failure and does not escalate, switch to recovery credentials or misclassify the result as protocol unsupported.

cases.given: Untrusted attribute names, targets and command-like strings
cases.when: Application configuration is validated
cases.then: Only approved targets, bounded names and explicit values reach adapters; shell/CLI injection and cross-device access are rejected.

cases.given: Malformed/mismatched XML, paging, oversized reads or a stalled server
cases.when: Discovery consumes untrusted responses
cases.then: It fails with bounded typed errors, no transcript success and no write requests.

cases.given: Unapproved device IDs, wrong credentials or a recovery identity
cases.when: Connection policy and authentication run
cases.then: Unapproved access is refused and failed authentication cannot cause fallback.

cases.given: Invalid 1.1 chunks or ambiguous/wrong-namespace XML envelopes
cases.when: The NETCONF codec decodes them
cases.then: Only bounded byte-counted frames and unambiguous protocol envelopes are accepted.

cases.given: An explicit unsupported read RPC or a network failure
cases.when: Transport selection is considered
cases.then: Only the unsupported operation gets the approved CLI supplement; network errors do not cause fallback or retries.

cases.given: Concurrent collections using immutable approved policy
cases.when: Six actual SSH/NETCONF sessions collect evidence
cases.then: Each returns read evidence and all server-side requests remain in the read-only allowlist.

cases.given: Generated Ed25519 and RSA client identities
cases.when: SSH authentication and read collection execute
cases.then: Public-key authentication succeeds using the pinned host, including RSA-SHA2, without mutable device operations.

cases.given: An approved unused slot on a synthetic SSH device with runtime-generated keys
cases.when: The explicit CSR adapter executes its bounded CLI dialogue
cases.then: One uniquely labelled non-exportable key command is sent, public CSR/signature/SAN/device-SPKI are verified and existing keys/configuration remain unchanged. Actual router write acceptance remains L-002.

cases.given: An occupied Trustpoint/key label, wrong image or unsynchronized time
cases.when: CSR preflight runs
cases.then: It rejects the target before opening a mutation shell; no key deletion, replacement, binding change or save command is available.

cases.given: Runtime-generated CA, recorded public CSR and issued leaves
cases.when: Public key, exact Subject/SAN, EKU/KeyUsage, lifetime or validity differs from the approved policy
cases.then: The pure validator rejects the certificate without an acceptance receipt; it has no device import or HTTPS switch capability. Live unchanged-binding evidence remains L-002.

cases.given: Explicit approved roots, intermediate bundle and immediate issuer pins
cases.when: A leaf-only response or returned chain is verified
cases.then: Leaf-only input requires the local approved path; missing paths, unknown roots, malformed/duplicate/unrelated certificates and unapproved issuers fail without system trust or network fetch.

cases.given: Distinct RA display label, technical template identity and a trusted synthetic enrollment snapshot
cases.when: The leaf template and current policy/principal/permission evidence are checked
cases.then: Wrong template name/OID/version, RA binding, principal, denied rights or stale evidence is rejected. Public CI verifies snapshot enforcement; actual AD permissions and template mapping remain private L-002 evidence.

cases.given: A stage-only gate, temporary SQLite and independent loopback TLS service
cases.when: Import succeeds, its reply is lost or the presented active certificate changes
cases.then: Fresh before/after handshakes preserve the baseline on success/lost reply, while changed TLS prevents STAGED/withKey; no HTTP payload is sent. Actual SSH forbidden-command assertions are S-026; live router acceptance remains L-002.

cases.given: Core push supplies a leaf without a chain field
cases.when: The connector resolves issuers
cases.then: It uses an approved public bundle reference and reports withKey only for a confirmed matching device key.

cases.given: Passwords, SSH keys, account secrets and request transcripts
cases.when: Any error or debug path logs
cases.then: Secrets and private key material are absent from logs/journal/metadata; audit events retain useful operation correlation.

cases.given: Generated public CSRs, expected DNS/Subject and reported device SPKI
cases.when: Signature, name, key size, exportability and input policy are checked
cases.then: Invalid signatures, extra names, wrong Subject/key/size, missing non-exportable proof, injection and duplicate SANs are rejected.

cases.given: A signed CSR with unrequested CA/IP content or another signature algorithm
cases.when: The CSR policy validator runs
cases.then: Unapproved extension content and non-SHA256 RSA signatures are rejected before CSR_READY.

cases.given: Real SQLite with a normalized CSR request and counting generator
cases.when: Calls overlap, retry or reopen the journal
cases.then: Only one generation is dispatched; verified CSR artifacts survive restart, caller mutations cannot alter cached bytes and changed specifications are rejected.

cases.given: Intent/completion write failure, timeout or invalid generator result
cases.when: The CSR gate runs and later reopens
cases.then: Failed intent never dispatches; unknown generation retains KEY_CREATING and service ownership without returning an uncommitted CSR or regenerating a key.

cases.given: Default-disabled writes or a weak RSA policy
cases.when: A CSR adapter is constructed
cases.then: Invalid or unapproved policy is rejected without authentication or mutation.

cases.given: A journal v1 operation without CSR artifacts
cases.when: Schema v2 is opened
cases.then: Migration preserves IDs/state/correlation/history and adds public CSR storage transactionally; invalid policy cannot reach a generator.

cases.given: A journal claiming schema v2 with its CSR table missing
cases.when: The store opens
cases.then: It refuses incomplete storage rather than reset or proceed to generation.

cases.given: A generator that mutates its received DNS-name slice
cases.when: The result is validated and recorded
cases.then: Copied canonical policy and persisted request remain unchanged.

cases.given: Replacement, timeout, AAA denial, unknown prompt, stderr, wrong SAN or exportable/reused key responses
cases.when: The synthetic SSH dialogue reaches generation
cases.then: The connection stops with no CSR result and no second key command; replacement is never confirmed.

cases.given: A changed host identity, protected slot, injected Subject or unapproved address
cases.when: CSR request policy is evaluated
cases.then: It fails before authentication or mutation and cannot redirect the write adapter.

cases.given: An unknown CSR generation outcome in the shared lifecycle gate
cases.when: The caller retries and requests reconciliation
cases.then: Only one generation occurred; reconciliation calls the read-only inspector and leaves uncertainty/service ownership intact.

cases.given: Checked time readings and mutable constructor inputs
cases.when: Synchronization/freshness/uncertainty fails or caller policy buffers change
cases.then: Unsafe clocks and cancelled requests fail; accepted policy DER, DNS names and template version pointers remain independent of caller mutation.

cases.given: V1 name and V2 OID/version encodings plus Microsoft Application Policies
cases.when: Missing/zero/max versions, malformed DER, conflicting names or extra purposes are supplied
cases.then: Exact version presence and valid technical-name forms work; negative/overflow/trailing/critical template content and non-serverAuth or qualified application policies fail.

cases.given: A leaf signed by the pinned intermediate
cases.when: That intermediate is expired, future-dated, restricted to other DNS names or restricted to client authentication
cases.then: A matching issuer pin cannot bypass complete path validity, name constraints or CA purpose restrictions.

cases.given: An immutable validator, saved CSR and public leaf
cases.when: Receipts expire, copied buffers change, invalid key proof/signature is supplied or validations run concurrently
cases.then: Zero/expired receipts and invalid recorded CSRs fail; receipt bytes/provenance are protected and concurrent validation succeeds under hosted race detection.

cases.given: Real SQLite with a recorded CSR and approved policy digest
cases.when: Raw digest, zero receipt, mismatched CSR, stale revision, storage failure or changed certificate attempts acceptance
cases.then: Only a fresh matching validator receipt atomically advances CERT_READY and history; rejected/failed attempts preserve state and cannot substitute a different bound leaf.

cases.given: The certificate gate using real SQLite and trusted synthetic evidence
cases.when: A wrong leaf is supplied, the valid leaf repeats or the journal restarts after enrollment permission is revoked
cases.then: Invalid input never advances state, same-leaf acceptance is idempotent and revoked permission blocks cached-leaf retry without changing the durable record.

cases.given: An existing active inventory plus an explicitly unenrolled empty Trustpoint
cases.when: Inventory is parsed after CSR preparation
cases.then: The empty slot is reported separately without fabricating a certificate; missing or mismatched enrollment notices remain incomplete.

cases.given: An opt-in pinned SSH adapter with a prepared CSR slot and runtime public certificates
cases.when: The CA authentication and identity import dialogues complete
cases.then: Exact public DER reaches only the reserved Trustpoint, dispatch checks repeat and independent key/readback matches; no activation, save, key or NETCONF mutation is issued.

cases.given: Unsynchronized NTP, wrong key binding, exportability, denial, overwrite, mismatched display fingerprint or incomplete reply
cases.when: The real SSH packet/dialogue adapter imports
cases.then: Unsafe preflight stops before writes; unverified acceptance is never confirmed and uncertain/stderr output cannot become success or leak diagnostics.

cases.given: Changed address, host key, policy, command-like slot, wrong leaf or disabled write policy
cases.when: The staging adapter validates its scope
cases.then: Unapproved inputs fail before authentication/mutation and unprotected ancestor references are rejected.

cases.given: An approved leaf-only input, saved device CSR, private bundle and temporary SQLite
cases.when: Staging completes and repeats after restart or current key evidence disappears
cases.then: The approved path is resolved without a caller chain, one import reaches STAGED and withKey requires fresh matching key evidence; cached state alone cannot report it. Core DTO wiring remains S-007/#13.

cases.given: Denied policy, wrong leaf, changed active binding/TLS, preexisting candidate, invalid state digest or missing key proof
cases.when: Runtime staging is requested
cases.then: It returns no withKey and dispatches no import; matching preexisting bytes without a prior intent are not adopted.

cases.given: A completed ACME issuance with a cancelled operation before staging or during its dispatch preparation
cases.when: The runtime gate reaches the final write authorization
cases.then: Cancellation is rechecked from durable state and prevents device import even though CERT_READY already exists.

cases.given: Real complete inventory parsing for empty/filled CSR slots and a multi-level CA chain
cases.when: Staging readback and explicit ancestor mapping are checked
cases.then: Active/candidate/issuer roles stay separate, the protected-state digest ignores only the owned slot, missing ancestors fail and inventory alone cannot fabricate private-key association.

cases.given: An otherwise approved SSH staging target whose dispatch authorizer denies access
cases.when: The concrete importer attempts to begin
cases.then: No public certificate or configuration write follows the denial and no activation/save path exists.

cases.given: Concurrent callers attempt the same stable HTTPS Location
cases.when: Begin requests race or renewal owners conflict
cases.then: One durable service owner admits one operation; a conflicting owner, stale revision or unsafe release is rejected before a mutation flow can start.

cases.given: Two internal API/worker gates, real SQLite and a counting importer
cases.when: The same operation and certificate overlap, retry or survive restart
cases.then: Exactly one importer call occurs; identical committed STAGED results are reused and uncertain IMPORTING requires reconciliation. Actual IOS XE import, certificate validation and live observation remain later acceptance.

cases.given: Durable operation correlation and current approved service policy
cases.when: An operation ID, entity, Location, device, target, host key, owner, policy, original fingerprint, staging name or revision is forged or stale
cases.then: Get/import/progression refuse mismatched correlation before dispatch; identical request retries and restart preserve the original operation.

cases.given: The switch succeeds but its response is lost
cases.when: The deadline expires
cases.then: The engine queries actual binding and new TLS before retry/rollback; timeout is never equated with no change.

cases.given: A crash at each durable-intent and side-effect boundary
cases.when: The process restarts
cases.then: It reconciles the existing operation and device state, preserving the original CSR/order/key rather than starting another renewal.

cases.given: New TLS validation fails after switching
cases.when: Rollback runs
cases.then: The old binding, fresh TLS old fingerprint and persistence are all verified before ROLLED_BACK; any failure becomes NEEDS_OPERATOR.

cases.given: The new leaf is active but saving configuration fails
cases.when: Completion is recorded
cases.then: The engine reports ACTIVE_NOT_PERSISTED, never COMMITTED, and retains recovery resources.

cases.given: Another administrator changes configuration after preflight
cases.when: The connector would globally save or recover
cases.then: It detects the conflict and stops for reconciliation without persisting or reverting unrelated changes.

cases.given: Real temporary SQLite storage with query-only, SQLITE_FULL, writer lock, cancellation or closed-database failure
cases.when: Import intent cannot commit
cases.then: The importer is never called and recorded CERT_READY/revision remain unchanged; failures do not authorize side effects.

cases.given: An active or retained rollback certificate/key
cases.when: Core remove, cancellation or stale-operation cleanup is requested
cases.then: Protected resources cannot be deleted and a verified recovery route remains available.

cases.given: Expected target address, SNI, chain and leaf SHA-256
cases.when: An independent fresh TLS probe runs
cases.then: Wrong host/chain/fingerprint, cached connections, clock errors and another endpoint cannot satisfy activation.

cases.given: One active subprocess with a committed IMPORTING intent on SQLite WAL/FULL
cases.when: Another instance opens the database and the original process is killed
cases.then: The second instance is refused while active; reopening recovers persistent service ownership and history without redispatch.

cases.given: A dispatched counting importer and a concurrent shutdown
cases.when: Close would release the OS instance lock
cases.then: Close waits for the callback and completion record; a second instance cannot enter while the callback is still running.

cases.given: An importer error or failed completion write after committed import intent
cases.when: The journal reopens and the same push retries
cases.then: IMPORTING and service ownership survive; the second importer call is forbidden and private diagnostic text is not returned.

cases.given: Persisted operations, approved owner/policy and foreign/future schema files
cases.when: Configuration changes while work is pending or storage is reopened
cases.then: Pending configuration cannot be replaced; old-policy references are rejected after a safe owner change; foreign/future databases are refused without resetting them.

cases.given: An operation whose state/revision no longer matches its committed history
cases.when: The journal starts
cases.then: It refuses inconsistent durable state instead of treating it as permission to repeat a side effect.

cases.given: Two approved HTTPS services and a caller-held configuration slice
cases.when: One importer blocks and the caller mutates its staging names
cases.then: The other service can begin independently and copied operator policy cannot be expanded by caller mutation.

cases.given: Unsafe owner/target/host identity/policy/Location/staging values or hard-linked database files
cases.when: Journal configuration and instance ownership are established
cases.then: Invalid bindings and file aliases are rejected; a second handle cannot bypass single-instance ownership.

cases.given: A lost reply after complete import or after only the issuer was installed
cases.when: The same operation resumes after SQLite reopen
cases.then: Complete independent evidence permits STAGED; partial evidence retains IMPORTING. Neither path repeats import or releases ownership.

cases.given: Concurrent runtime pushes or enrollment permission revoked just before the adapter's dispatch check
cases.when: The same operation attempts import
cases.then: One worker proceeds, overlaps return busy and newly denied permission prevents a stale receipt from authorizing a write.

cases.given: Real SQLite triggers denying artifact/intent/completion or changed settings/protected state
cases.when: Staging fails and restarts
cases.then: Failed intent permits no import; lost completion recovers read-only, changed bindings fail and storage diagnostics do not escape.

cases.given: An operation with an actual recorded CSR and validated leaf
cases.when: The old digest-only foundation import entry point is used
cases.then: It refuses dispatch; runtime imports require fresh receipt, bound artifacts and current device/TLS verification.

cases.given: A v4 journal containing the original ready CSR operation
cases.when: Schema migrates to v5 or a staged operation loses its artifact row
cases.then: Migration preserves the operation; missing import provenance prevents startup without resetting or guessing successful deployment.

cases.given: A dispatched runtime import with concurrent Store.Close
cases.when: Fresh authorization, readback and completion run while shutdown waits
cases.then: The OS ownership lock stays held, dispatch rechecks do not deadlock and restart validates the result without another import.

cases.given: A saved public device CSR, separate ACME signer, real temporary SQLite and loopback HTTPS ACME server
cases.when: Signed account/order/challenge/finalize/POST-as-GET calls complete
cases.then: The server verifies JWS/KID/JWK and exact original CSR bytes; one order/finalize reaches certificate-policy CERT_READY. Production code generates no certificate key; real DNS and ILM acceptance remain separate.

cases.given: Directory metadata, exact CSR identifiers and actual challenge offers
cases.when: EAB-required new provisioning, HTTP-only offers, wrong identifiers, foreign endpoints or a bad leaf is returned
cases.then: Unapproved flows cannot reach CERT_READY; unsupported authorization cannot present DNS or finalize. Disabled EAB still requires account signing and complete domain authorization.

cases.given: A badNonce response followed by 429 with Retry-After
cases.when: The bounded client retries and the worker resumes
cases.then: The retry uses the response-provided nonce and same payload; cooldown persists, early calls perform no network I/O and recovery creates only one actual order/finalize.

cases.given: Server-side issuance followed by a lost finalize response
cases.when: The actual SQLite journal is closed/reopened and the engine resumes
cases.then: It fetches the recorded original order and certificate, revalidates through the certificate gate and never creates another order or repeats finalize.

cases.given: Foreign multi-chunk TXT values and a separate ownership-marker RRset in a verified multi-value configuration
cases.when: Presentation and reference-only cleanup are retried
cases.then: Only the operation's exact value and marker are added/deleted once; foreign values survive. Actual ILM multi-value validation remains K-002/private #15.

cases.given: A fake clock with renewal window, jitter, timezone and downtime
cases.when: The worker schedules or restarts
cases.then: It renews within policy once, applies bounded backoff and cannot overlap Core native renewal.

cases.given: Deployment is committed but ILM inventory sync fails
cases.when: Sync retries
cases.then: The connector retries inventory sync without reissuing or redeploying the already committed certificate.

cases.given: An authorized ACME-owned operation with saved CSR/account/order association
cases.when: The journal reopens or stale revisions and changed account/order identities are supplied
cases.then: Original CSR and resource URLs survive; binding replacement and CAS replay are rejected.

cases.given: A v2 journal with CSR artifacts or an incomplete v3 schema
cases.when: The store migrates or opens
cases.then: Migration preserves CSR/operation correlation, while missing ACME storage fails startup without resetting state.

cases.given: Native Core ownership, missing CSR, unsafe resource URLs or unavailable writes
cases.when: ACME association, intent or overlapping run is requested
cases.then: Owner/CSR/HTTPS profile boundaries and committed intent are mandatory; concurrent workers cannot enter the same operation.

cases.given: An accepted new-order request whose response and order URL were lost
cases.when: The caller retries the operation
cases.then: ORDER_CREATING remains unresolved; repeated calls require reconciliation and cannot create a replacement order.

cases.given: An original order still processing and a zero Retry-After poll response
cases.when: Bounded attempts run and the server later marks the order valid
cases.then: Only one finalize occurs, polling does not spin and the same order/certificate is recovered.

cases.given: HTTP-date rate limits or finite nonce/attempt budgets
cases.when: Retries are scheduled or budgets end
cases.then: Date delays are not shortened and bounded retries retain unfinished ownership without further issuance.

cases.given: Overlapping engine calls or an actual SQLite trigger rejecting order intent
cases.when: Protocol work is requested
cases.then: Only one worker enters and a failed order-intent write permits no order, finalize or solver dispatch.

cases.given: Invalid policy/reference/timeout, insecure TLS or a cancelled caller
cases.when: The engine is constructed or run
cases.then: Unsafe configuration/cancellation cannot initiate network I/O and policy digest must match the certificate gate.

cases.given: Lost account-registration response or throttled certificate download after issuance
cases.when: The engine resumes using the same key and saved operation
cases.then: Account lookup/download recovery keeps one registration, one order and one finalize.

cases.given: A Directory endpoint returning a redirect into another profile
cases.when: Discovery runs
cases.then: Only the original URL is requested; the redirect cannot register an account or create an order.

cases.given: Recorded synthetic challenge intents and a now-expired original order
cases.when: The worker resumes
cases.then: It asks the backend to clean only recorded owned intents, retains INVALID and does not finalize or create a replacement. Real TXT cleanup remains A-005.

cases.given: A per-attempt HTTP request budget too small for the entire initial workflow
cases.when: Progress is resumed after bounded deferrals
cases.then: Every attempt respects the wire request limit and eventual acceptance still has one original order and one finalize.

cases.given: An approved ACME challenge and real temporary SQLite
cases.when: The claim progresses, revisions replay and the store restarts
cases.then: Exact challenge value, target binding and random sidecar marker survive; stale revisions and presentation after cleanup fail.

cases.given: A v3 journal with an existing ACME challenge
cases.when: It migrates to v4 or required ownership storage is absent
cases.then: Migration preserves original association and permits a bound claim; missing v4 storage fails startup rather than resetting state.

cases.given: Two approved operations sharing one DNS owner in explicit multi-value mode
cases.when: Presentations race and each operation cleans independently
cases.then: CAS prerequisites preserve both challenge values and one cleanup cannot remove the other's TXT.

cases.given: An applied ADD with lost reply and then an applied DELETE with lost reply
cases.when: SQLite reopens and reference-only cleanup resumes
cases.then: Signed-read ownership semantics permit exact recovery without a second ADD or broad delete; each mutation occurs once.

cases.given: A preexisting equivalent value or an unconfirmed ADD whose value is absent
cases.when: Presentation or cleanup runs
cases.then: Existing data is never adopted/deleted and absence cannot resolve an unknown pending ADD; the original claim remains for reconciliation.

cases.given: Single-TXT conflicts, propagation delay, permission denial, forged scope or a canceled applied ADD
cases.when: The solver presents and explicit cleanup follows
cases.then: Unsafe views/scope cannot add data; propagation does not repeat ADD; cancellation cleanup removes only the recorded pair.

cases.given: A loopback TCP authoritative DNS peer and synthetic MIC context
cases.when: Actual RFC2136 add/delete packets and signed minimal replies execute
cases.then: Both names carry full-set prerequisites atomically, deletion uses class NONE exact TXT RDATA, foreign chunks survive and every authoritative request is signed. This is packet evidence, not live Kerberos acceptance.

cases.given: Unsigned answers, aliases, signed refusal, credential errors or an unapproved read name
cases.when: The concrete TCP adapter handles them
cases.then: It rejects unsafe evidence and foreign targets without changing records or leaking private diagnostics; no unsigned authentication fallback exists.

cases.given: Synthetic initiator/MIC contexts and loopback TKEY replies
cases.when: Final signatures are absent/tampered, mutual establishment fails, tokens exceed bounds or continuations repeat
cases.then: Only mutually completed, correctly signed original final packets establish the adapter; token and continuation budgets are enforced. A real AD KDC remains #15.

cases.given: Explicit realm/account/password and raw AES-only krb5 configuration
cases.when: KDC discovery, weak enctypes, unsafe/missing credentials or diagnostic formatting are attempted
cases.then: Unsafe input is rejected before KDC access and credential formatting/JSON is redacted; ambient credentials and NTLM are not used.

cases.given: Caller cancellation after a challenge presentation with optional cleanup denial
cases.when: The workflow cleans and restarts using the same journal
cases.then: CancelRequested is durable, restart retries only cleanup and no order/finalize or already completed cleanup is replayed.

cases.given: A real SQLite trigger denying the ADDING intent
cases.when: The solver attempts presentation
cases.then: No DNS mutation follows the failed commit and private storage diagnostics do not escape.

cases.given: A missing owner marker, altered TXT chunking or a concurrent foreign value
cases.when: Cleanup tries to remove its own records
cases.then: Unproven ownership/encoding prevents deletion; prerequisite conflict recovery preserves the competing foreign value.

cases.given: Invalid target/view/credential references or caller-mutated configuration
cases.when: The provider is constructed or an unfinished claim is cleaned under a changed view
cases.then: Unsafe inputs fail, copied scope remains fixed and unfinished DNS ownership cannot be rebound.

cases.given: An active DNS claim whose ACME operation is cancelled
cases.when: A direct presentation retry or exact cleanup is requested
cases.then: Cancellation prevents presentation before any DNS session but permits cleanup of the original recorded pair.

cases.given: Configured loopback resolver views with multiple TXT values or an alias
cases.when: Visibility is checked in single/multi-value mode
cases.then: Single-TXT rejects coexistence, explicit multi-value mode can observe the expected value and aliases never redirect the lookup.

cases.given: A loopback TCP DNS peer that withholds its reply
cases.when: A caller without a deadline cancels the context
cases.then: The connection closes promptly without waiting for the longer configured exchange timeout. Upstream KDC APIs remain separately uninterruptible.
